_comment: THE FINISHER IS STILL IN THE SIDEBOARD, one Living Wish away -- the deck's actual kill chain,
and the longest route the button is allowed to promise. ScanHandSinks' wish route prices the
wish {1}{G} plus the fetched creature as hand_setup_mv; ComboFinishFromHand casts the wish,
fetches BY NAME (not by resolution-time ranking, which is the seed-7 divergence this whole
gate was rebuilt around) and deploys it, all inside the go-off the button applies.
The Emiel outlet is what makes it reachable at all: the wish costs green, the deck-out costs
colourless, and the Displacer would have eaten the only pip a pass produces.
_history_comment: USER, 2026-09-10: 'Combo Off needs to list exactly how we reached the win. It should not list
"Combo Off" in the history except potentially to show when the user clicked it.' So the
narration the viewer renders -- the engine's own event stream during the apply -- has to name
every action, and must contain no macro standing in for the line. This is the LONGEST chain the
deck has (wish -> fetch -> cast -> exile the library), which makes it the right fixture to pin
it on: the blink WITH ITS OUTLET, the Living Wish and what it fetched, the deck-out itself.
expect_history_no_macro defaults true, so every combo-off fixture is guarded against a macro
creeping back in; only this one asserts the contents.
expect_history_contains: Emiel the Blessed: blinked Cloud of Faeries
